title: Provider SLA Measurement (Latency, Jitter, Loss to PE)
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Provider SLA Measurement (Latency, Jitter, Loss to PE)' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_provider_sla_measurement_latency_jitter_loss_to_` (UC-5.10.11), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Provider SLA Measurement (Latency, Jitter, Loss to PE)", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=target_index` sourcetype='target_sourcetype' where `server.address` satisfies `avg_loss_pct` > 0.5 for UC-5.10.11 ('Provider SLA Measurement (Latency, Jitter, Loss to PE)'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.

dataSources: `index=thousandeyes_metrics sourcetype=cisco:thousandeyes:metric` from Enterprise Agents probing carrier PE addresses (`server.address`) via Tests Stream — Metrics in `ta_cisco_thousandeyes` (Splunkbase #7719). Uses OTel-style metrics `network.latency` (seconds), `network.jitter` (milliseconds), `network.loss` (percent). Optional alternate: Cisco IOS IP SLA SNMP traps forwarded into Splunk.
app: `ta_cisco_thousandeyes` — Cisco ThousandEyes App for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7719](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7719)), Cisco Supported.
spl:
`stream_index` thousandeyes.test.type="agent-to-server"
| stats avg(network.latency) as avg_latency_sec avg(network.jitter) as avg_jitter_ms avg(network.loss) as avg_loss_pct latest(thousandeyes.source.agent.name) as agent_site by server.address
| lookup carrier_pe_targets.csv pe_ip AS server.address OUTPUT carrier_name sla_latency_ms sla_jitter_ms sla_loss_pct circuit_id
| eval avg_latency_ms=round(avg_latency_sec*1000,2)
| eval latency_violation=if(isnotnull(sla_latency_ms) AND avg_latency_ms>sla_latency_ms,1,0)
| eval jitter_violation=if(isnotnull(sla_jitter_ms) AND avg_jitter_ms>sla_jitter_ms,1,0)
| eval loss_violation=if(isnotnull(sla_loss_pct) AND avg_loss_pct>sla_loss_pct,1,0)
| where latency_violation=1 OR jitter_violation=1 OR loss_violation=1 OR avg_loss_pct>0.5 OR avg_latency_ms>80
| table agent_site carrier_name circuit_id server.address avg_latency_ms avg_jitter_ms avg_loss_pct sla_latency_ms sla_jitter_ms sla_loss_pct
| sort -avg_loss_pct
description: Pulls synthetic probe metrics aimed at each carrier provider-edge endpoint and compares rolling averages against contractual latency, jitter, and packet-loss ceilings encoded in lookup tables—surfacing degradation before subscriber-facing alarms trigger.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `target_index`** — Planned work for 'Provider SLA Measurement (Latency, Jitter, Loss to PE)' shifts `avg` over `span=1h` while `server.address` remains in-scope for UC-5.10.11. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `avg_latency_ms` without crossing `avg_loss_pct` > 0.5. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `server.address`** — Health checks in `target_index` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `configured_sourcetype`** — First 48h baseline for `server.address` is unstable; join `carrier_pe_targets.csv` prior to threshold.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `server.address`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Completed ThousandEyes OAuth onboarding plus Tests Stream — Metrics input landing in `thousandeyes_metrics`.
• Accurate inventory tying probe agents to geographic markets so latency budgets reflect distance.
• Contract annex listing numeric SLA thresholds per product (often differentiated for consumer versus enterprise tails).
• Splunk macros translating metric names when tenants remain on legacy v1 schemas.

Step 1 — Create agent-to-server tests enumerating each PE IP with ICMP or lightweight TCP where ICMP blocked—document chosen protocol in lookup to avoid apples-to-oranges comparisons.

Step 2 — Validate metric presence using short-window `mpreview` or `tstats` (metrics pipeline) ensuring `network.latency`, `network.jitter`, `network.loss` populate.

Step 3 — Join `carrier_pe_targets.csv` supplying carrier_name, circuit identifiers, and SLA numbers; implement composite alerting requiring two consecutive fifteen-minute breaches before paging.

Step 4 — Publish dashboard pairing Splunk charts with deep links to ThousandEyes views for carrier collaboration calls.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting: agents behind NAT may skew latency—relocate agents; PE ICMP de-prioritization exaggerates loss—switch to TCP-based tests; macro drift between Cloud vs Enterprise agents requires periodic validation scripts.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`ta_cisco_thousandeyes` — Cisco ThousandEyes App for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7719](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7719)), Cisco Supported.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`avg_latency_ms, avg_loss_pct, carrier_name sla_latency_ms sla_jitter_ms sla_loss_pct circuit_id, jitter_violation`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
